detail:
Full summary: Pre-tag review of the 2.14.0 diff confirmed 8 findings (1 major: lifecycle_reverts false-positives on sanctioned downgrades); all fixed TDD — detector narrowed to overridden/superseded, override read-back race-tolerant, persisted checked at all 5 remaining call sites, revert count surfaced in ingest summaries. 1637 green.
Decisions: Chose to arm the revert detector only for db-status overridden/superseded (REVERT_WATCHED) — those have no sanctioned undo verb, so a file-wins downgrade is either branch divergence or a discarded write; active→provisional (reconsider) and archived→anything (unarchive) are first-class flows that legitimately arrive via git and were firing false alarms in the exact channel field users will watch. Message now names both remaining causes. Alternative rejected: extras-presence heuristics — fragile across mixed-version stores.; Chose to make override's read-back race-tolerant: PERSIST_FAILED only when the write did not persist or the record is gone; a concurrent status flip after a persisted write is echoed honestly in result.status (type widened to DecisionStatus) — the reviewers proved the old check threw a false 'Nothing was recorded' and silently skipped replacement-decision creation when a same-id writer raced.; Chose to check {persisted} at all five remaining updateStatus call sites (promote→not_found, decide supersedes flip→supersedes_dangling, archive_stale→not_found, unarchive→not_found, housekeeping bulk promote→counted only when persisted) — closes the D14 affirmative-on-no-op shape everywhere, routing failures into each caller's existing failure lane rather than inventing new ones.; Chose reconsider clearing promoted_by/promoted_at on demotion while override/supersede KEEP them — a provisional awaiting re-ratification must not carry a ratification stamp, but retired records keep it as history (overridden_by marks the terminal actor).; Chose log-surface only for lifecycle_reverts this release (both ingest summaries now include the count; OVERRIDE-03 reworded to say server log) — an MCP-visible surface (status/housekeeping field) would be better but needs a shape decision; recorded as follow-up, not slipped into the release.
Findings: 7th consecutive pre-tag review to catch real defects — including a major in code the SAME session wrote hours earlier under review pressure; the practice pays for itself even on fix-rounds of fix-rounds; need: MCP-visible surface for lifecycle_reverts (status or housekeeping result field) so agents — not just log-tailing humans — see discarded lifecycle writes; log parity shipped in 2.14.0; Review sub-finding accepted as-is: lost UPGRADE writes (discarded unarchive/reconsider) are invisible to the downgrade-only heuristic — inherent to the design; the detector is a tripwire for the dangerous direction, not a ledger
